title: Building Trust and Driving Improvement Through Manufacturing
summary: Continuous improvement applies to more than manufacturing processes at Sonoco. It’s the mindset of an effective leader.
body_markdown:
Lauren Hughes, Converting Manufacturing Operations Manager


Converting Manufacturing Operations Manager, Lauren Hughes, recently received a 2026 SCBIZ Women Powering Manufacturing Award for her meaningful contributions to manufacturing. Her reputation for being a strong leader who builds trust and drives continuous improvement vividly demonstrates the Sonoco spirit of ‘People Build Businesses by Doing the Right Thing.’


As we end Manufacturing Month, we asked Hughes to highlight her thoughts on the industry, leadership, this award and more.


### **What excites you about working in manufacturing?**


I see manufacturing as an opportunity to improve people’s lives in tangible ways. It may seem mundane to others, but I’ve found that every day is different. As an operations leader, I’m energized by having the opportunity to network across teams, build strong relationships and drive continuous improvement.


### **What is one improvement you’re most proud of your team for achieving?**


On top of the team achieving Sonoco Performance System (SPS) Gold, seeing everyone embrace continuous improvement and keep raising the bar has been especially rewarding. In addition, improving the employee experience has been a highlight of my team here.


As the plant manager, I’m working hard to equip employees and motivate continuous growth by aligning daily activities with SPS standards, encouraging data-driven decision-making and fostering cross-functional collaboration. I’m excited to see what we accomplish together as a team in the days ahead.


### **How have other leaders shaped your leadership approach?**


Lauren Hughes guides a Sonoco summer intern around the warehouse.


When I met Ernest Haynes (President, Global Consumer Packaging) years ago at a college career fair, I was quickly impressed by how well he treated me. Even though he was a regional manager at the time, he listened, showed empathy and prioritized fairness. His real-life example of living the Sonoco culture helped me see firsthand how high-functioning teams result from building a high level of trust.


Early in my career, I worked for another leader who set a strong example of accountability—taking responsibility instead of assigning blame. His approach to people management shaped my own. Balancing accountability and care for people, I learned to create and communicate clear expectations, stand firm in my position and hold people to the set expectations.


Later in my career, a very strong female leader demonstrated the importance of a clear but firm communication style. Manufacturing is a male-dominated field, but women don’t have to raise their voice to earn respect. By saying what I mean and meaning what I say and being patient with others’ different approaches, I can build respect and create a space for employees to voice their opinions.


### **What does receiving a Woman Powering Manufacturing award mean to you?**


It’s deeply meaningful. It recognizes not only my individual efforts but also the progress women in this traditionally male-dominated industry are making. I feel motivated to continue advocating, mentoring and serving as an example of women impactfully leading, innovating and succeeding.


To those at Sonoco who’ve invested in me, I’m very grateful for their trust and support, and I remain committed to doing my very best to represent the Company and my plant team well.
